question: Why is checking drug compatibility important when administering multiple intravenous infusions?

options.A: Incompatible drugs can react and form solid crystals that block the catheter
options.B: Combining medications changes the colour of the plastic infusion tubing
options.C: Mixing drugs always causes the patient to develop a skin rash
options.D: Incompatible solutions neutralize each other and make nurses look careless

explanation: Chemical reactions between mixed drugs can create precipitates that clog the line and endanger the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to care for an FGM survivor in the clinic?

options.A: Reporting the adult patient to local police immediately
options.B: Inspecting the surgical site without warning the patient
options.C: Refusing to discuss the cultural background of the practice
options.D: Using a trauma-informed and non-judgmental approach

explanation: Great choice! Trauma-informed care builds trust, lowers anxiety, and makes sure the patient feels safe and respected.

question: What is the hallmark feature of personality disorders?

options.A: Severe memory loss caused by acute physical brain trauma
options.B: Rigid, enduring patterns of behavior differing from cultural norms
options.C: Sudden temporary episodes of visual and auditory hallucinations
options.D: Rapid daily shifts between severe mania and deep depression

explanation: Personality disorders involve long-term, inflexible ways of thinking and acting that make daily relationships and coping quite tough.

question: Why is addiction considered a chronic brain disease instead of just a lack of willpower?

options.A: It permanently alters brain circuits related to reward and self-control
options.B: It only affects people with inherited genetic weaknesses in their lungs
options.C: It completely stops the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: It causes immediate physical paralysis in every single user

explanation: Think of it this way: long-term substance use physically changes how the brain's wiring works, making self-control super difficult without proper support. It's a health condition, not a character flaw!

question: Which stinging insect leaves its barbed stinger and venom sac behind in human skin?

options.A: Hornet
options.B: Wasp
options.C: Honeybee
options.D: Fire ant

explanation: Great job! The honeybee's stinger is barbed like a hook, so it anchors firmly into the skin and tears away from the bee's body along with the venom sac.

question: What chemical alarm is released by damaged tissues to make blood vessels open up during inflammation?

options.A: Histamine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: Well done! When cells get hurt, they release histamine. This chemical sounds the alarm, making blood vessels wider so white blood cells can rush easily to the rescue.

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance at the primary health care level?

options.A: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.B: To collect taxes from patients seeking medical treatment
options.C: To detect unusual increases in cases early and report them
options.D: To construct new hospital buildings in rural districts

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on health patterns so health workers can spot a sudden spike before it becomes a major outbreak.

question: A patient getting subcutaneous heparin complains of mild skin irritation at the injection site. What should you do?

options.A: Switch the patient to oral aspirin to bypass the skin route
options.B: Stop all future doses of heparin immediately without telling the doctor
options.C: Massage the injection site vigorously to spread the medication faster
options.D: Apply a warm compress and avoid rubbing the site to prevent bruising

explanation: Never massage a heparin injection site! Massaging can burst tiny blood vessels underneath and cause a nasty bruise or hematoma. Just rotate your sites!

question: What is the easiest and most reliable way to track rapid fluid loss in a patient with diarrhoea?

options.A: Daily body weight measurements
options.B: Body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Changes in skin color on the face
options.D: Total number of hours slept per night

explanation: Weight drops fast when you lose body water. Hopping on the scale daily is one of the best ways to catch dangerous dehydration early.

question: You check a patient's blood pressure during a routine community outreach. Which level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Spot-on! Screening tests like blood pressure checks catch hidden problems early. That is the exact definition of secondary prevention.

question: When can palliative care be started for someone with a serious illness?

options.A: Only when the patient is discharged back home
options.B: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.C: After all medical treatments have completely failed
options.D: Early in the disease course alongside curative treatments

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the very end! It can start right from diagnosis, walking hand-in-hand with treatments meant to cure or manage the disease.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen during untreated status epilepticus?

options.A: Extremely high body temperature from muscle activity
options.B: Dangerous buildup of acid in the body fluids
options.C: Severe oxygen shortage and brain tissue damage
options.D: Permanent drop in resting heart rate and low blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Instead of dropping, the heart rate and blood pressure actually shoot up due to extreme stress on the body. You're learning fast!

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Before touching a patient who has intact skin
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: When entering a clean general medical ward
options.D: After taking a patient's temperature with a digital thermometer

explanation: Spot on! Alcohol rubs are great, but they can't wash away physical dirt. When your hands look or feel dirty, good old soap and water is a must.

question: What is the primary goal of a respiratory assessment?

options.A: To check the client for peripheral edema
options.B: To evaluate oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange
options.C: To determine the primary cause of a heart attack
options.D: To measure the exact lung capacity in liters

explanation: Respiratory assessment focuses directly on how well the lungs are moving air and exchanging gases to keep tissues oxygenated. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must nurses and doctors strictly avoid inserting fingers into the vagina (digital exam) when placenta praevia is suspected?

options.A: It will immediately cause the baby to drop into a breech position
options.B: It introduces severe bacterial infection into the amniotic sac
options.C: It can disrupt the placenta and trigger massive, life-threatening bleeding
options.D: It causes the uterine muscle to contract into painful spasms

explanation: Touching the lower segment through the vagina can tear the low-lying placenta and cause severe hemorrhage. Knowing this safety rule keeps mothers safe!

question: Why should a nurse gently press the inner corner of the eye (punctal occlusion) right after giving eye drops?

options.A: To make the eye produce more fluid
options.B: To clean away sticky discharge
options.C: To keep the medicine from getting into the rest of the body
options.D: To keep the pupil wide open

explanation: Great job! Pressing the tear duct blocks the drop from draining down into the nose and entering the bloodstream, preventing unwanted side effects.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective nursing management planning?

options.A: Limited time due to busy daily duties
options.B: Excessive availability of reliable data
options.C: Staff resistance to clinical changes
options.D: Severe shortage of financial resources

explanation: Reliable data helps planning; the barrier is actually a lack of information, not an excess of good data. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is general supportive care often more critical than finding an antidote right away when someone is poisoned?

options.A: Supportive care keeps vital organs working while the body clears the toxin
options.B: Most poisons have strong antidotes available immediately
options.C: Antidotes only work if given within two minutes of exposure
options.D: Antidotes are too expensive to keep in most rural hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Since we don't have a magical antidote for every single poison out there, keeping the patient's breathing and heart going buys enough time for their body to naturally process and clear the toxin.

question: What must happen for a child to be born with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Only the mother needs to have the full sickle cell disease
options.B: The child must be exposed to severe malaria during infancy
options.C: Both parents must pass on a copy of the mutated sickle cell gene
options.D: Either parent must have genotype AS while the other has genotype AA

explanation: Because it is an autosomal recessive condition, a child needs two copies of the abnormal gene, requiring both parents to contribute a sickle gene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: A patient walks with an unsteady gait and cannot easily touch their finger to their nose. Which area is likely affected?

options.A: Medulla oblongata
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: When balance and smooth coordination are off during physical tests, it points straight to the cerebellum.

question: Which of these options is NOT a workplace hazard that threatens reproductive health?

options.A: Working around sources of ionizing radiation
options.B: Handling organic solvents in factories
options.C: Daily consumption of pasteurized milk
options.D: Prolonged exposure to heavy metals like lead

explanation: Easy peasy! Pasteurized milk is a healthy drink, not a toxic workplace chemical. Keep flying through these questions—you've got this!

question: What is the primary target group for public or community-funded nurseries?

options.A: Children who have already graduated from primary school
options.B: Low-income families and vulnerable populations who need subsidized support
options.C: Exclusively infants who require long-term neonatal intensive care
options.D: Only high-earning corporate executives seeking elite private tutors

explanation: Public and community nurseries are usually subsidized by governments or NGOs to ensure affordable childcare access for families with limited resources. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: What special X-ray technology does the radiologist use to watch the barium move in real-time?

options.A: Thermography
options.B: Electrocardiography
options.C: Fluoroscopy
options.D: Magnetic resonance

explanation: Keep it up! Fluoroscopy is basically an X-ray movie, letting the doctor watch the drink flow through your system live. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer comes in with a swollen right leg and dull flank pain. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Metastatic spread of cancer cells to the bones of the foot
options.B: Tumor compression of pelvic veins and the ureter
options.C: Development of deep vein thrombosis from excessive physical activity
options.D: Severe systemic dehydration caused by heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Makes sense when you picture it: a growing tumor in the pelvis can press against nearby blood vessels (causing leg swelling) and block the tubes leading from the kidneys, known as the ureters (causing flank pain).

question: Which hormones flood the body right away during a sudden 'fight-or-flight' moment?

options.A: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.B: Epinephrine and norepinephrine
options.C: Estrogen and progesterone
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: When you get a sudden fright, your adrenal medulla instantly pumps out adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline to get your body ready to run or fight!

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?

options.A: Living in cold climates
options.B: Advanced age
options.C: Eating too much red meat
options.D: Cracking your knuckles

explanation: Getting older is the primary risk factor because joint cartilage naturally weakens and loses its shock-absorbing ability over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: If a mother is still passing bright red lochia rubra on her fifth day postpartum, what might this mean?

options.A: The expected start of the mother's normal menstrual cycle
options.B: Normal progression of postpartum vaginal discharge
options.C: A potential delay or complication in normal uterine healing
options.D: Complete closure of the internal cervical os

explanation: Normally, bright red discharge only lasts for the first couple of days before turning brownish or pink. Seeing bright red blood on day five is a red flag that healing might be delayed or some tissue was retained. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: What is the very first thing you need to do before drawing a scatter diagram?

options.A: Coloring the data points with bright markers
options.B: Gathering paired data for the variables
options.C: Calculating the final correlation coefficient
options.D: Drawing the title at the top of the page

explanation: You have to collect your matching pairs of data first before you can plot anything on a graph. Step by step!

question: When should you collect a midstream urine sample for a lab culture if the patient needs antibiotics?

options.A: On the final day of the antibiotic course
options.B: Forty-eight hours after starting antibiotics
options.C: It does not matter when the sample is collected
options.D: Before giving the very first dose of antibiotic

explanation: Always collect the sample first! If you start antibiotics before taking the sample, the drug will kill the bacteria in the lab dish and give you a false negative result.

question: What shape does a standard antibody molecule look like?

options.A: Y-shape
options.B: Ring shape
options.C: Flat sheet
options.D: Spiral helix

explanation: Antibodies are shaped like the letter 'Y'. The tips of the Y have variable sites that lock specifically onto matching foreign antigens.

question: What is the main goal of community health campaigns led by nurses regarding early marriage?

options.A: To establish private hospitals exclusively for pediatric care
options.B: To fine families who host traditional wedding ceremonies
options.C: To force local religious leaders to step down from office
options.D: To challenge harmful cultural norms and educate families on health risks

explanation: You've got it! Education changes mindsets and tackles the root beliefs that keep the practice of early marriage alive.

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is the cervix?

options.A: The lower part of the uterus connecting to the vagina
options.B: The muscular wall of the main uterine body
options.C: The inner lining where a fertilized egg implants
options.D: The coiled tubes that transport eggs to the uterus

explanation: Spot on! The cervix forms the lower, cylindrical neck of the uterus that opens right into the vaginal canal. You've got this!

question: What is a major health risk for homebound clients who experience long-term loneliness and social isolation?

options.A: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Improved short-term memory function
options.C: Enhanced cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Weakened immune responses and cognitive decline

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of interaction takes a heavy toll on both body and mind, making it easier to fall sick and harder to stay sharp.

question: What should a polyvalent nurse do if standard supplies run out during an emergency?

options.A: Abandon the patient until fresh supplies arrive
options.B: Use problem-solving skills to find safe alternatives
options.C: Wait for the hospital director to fix the issue
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for the shortage

explanation: Well done! Resourcefulness is key in nursing. Finding safe alternatives keeps patients protected even when supplies are low.

question: In which layer of the uterus do fibroids usually start growing?

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Perimetrium
options.D: Cervix

explanation: The myometrium is the thick muscular middle layer of the uterus, which makes it the perfect home for fibroids to develop.

question: What main process causes osmotic diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid muscle contractions moving food too fast to digest
options.B: Unabsorbed particles staying in the gut and drawing water in
options.C: Bacterial toxins directly forcing salt and water secretion
options.D: Bleeding ulcers leaking protein and blood into the bowel

explanation: Osmotic means pulling water! When certain substances aren't absorbed in your gut, they act like a magnet, drawing water right along with them into your stool.

question: How does good birth spacing directly help a child survive and stay healthy?

options.A: By automatically increasing household monthly income and food production
options.B: By eliminating the transmission of all known genetic disorders
options.C: By giving the mother's body time to recover and rebuild essential nutrient stores
options.D: By ensuring older siblings graduate from secondary school first

explanation: Spot on! When a mother's body gets enough time to rest and rebuild nutrients between pregnancies, she is stronger and better equipped to nourish her next baby.

question: Which breathing sign is a classic warning of severe respiratory distress in a newborn?

options.A: Regular periodic breathing
options.B: Expiratory grunting
options.C: Deep abdominal snoring
options.D: Slow, quiet inspirations

explanation: When a baby makes a grunting sound as they breathe out, it's their way of trying to keep their tiny air sacs (alveoli) open. It's a red flag that they are struggling to breathe.

question: What does the term 'intersectionality' mean in healthcare?

options.A: The intersection of rural roads leading to a clinic
options.B: A meeting point between doctors and community leaders
options.C: How gender overlaps with poverty, age, and disability
options.D: The physical crossing of blood vessels in the heart

explanation: Intersectionality simply means looking at the whole person—how things like gender, age, and poverty combine to create unique challenges. Great concept to know as a nurse!

question: Which joint condition is a chronic autoimmune disease where the body attacks its own synovial membranes?

options.A: Ligament sprain
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Joint dislocation
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: You got it! Rheumatoid arthritis happens when the immune system mistakenly attacks joint tissues, leading to painful swelling.

question: Which of these is NOT the right way to handle workplace violence in a hospital?

options.A: Using de-escalation techniques to calm an agitated patient
options.B: Ensuring an easy exit route is available during a patient interview
options.C: Accepting physical abuse quietly because it is part of the job
options.D: Reporting all threatening incidents to hospital security and management

explanation: Violence is never part of the job description. If someone threatens or abuses you, report it and use your hospital's security protocols immediately.

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node before heading down to the ventricles?

options.A: To let the heart take a quick rest between beats
options.B: To send extra blood back up into the lungs
options.C: To give the ventricles enough time to fill completely with blood
options.D: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the atria

explanation: That tiny pause is super important! It ensures the top chambers (atria) finish squeezing all their blood down into the bottom chambers before the ventricles pump it away.

question: What is a major benefit of Tai Chi for older adults at risk of falling?

options.A: It rapidly increases total body bone density
options.B: It improves balance through slow, controlled movements
options.C: It eliminates the need for any assistive devices
options.D: It cures chronic joint inflammation in the knees

explanation: Tai Chi trains neuromuscular control and core stability, making it one of the most effective exercises for fall prevention. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h5)

question: Why must nurses encourage frequent feeding for a newborn undergoing treatment for jaundice?

options.A: Sucking on the breast helps strengthen the neck muscles against stiffness
options.B: Feeding provides extra calories to help the liver produce more red blood cells
options.C: Milk intake cools the digestive tract and prevents stomach irritation from lights
options.D: Regular feeds promote bowel movements, which help clear bilirubin out of the body

explanation: Frequent feeds mean regular bowel movements, and that is the main way the baby's body passes out the broken-down bilirubin. Feedings are treatment too!

question: What is your main nursing worry when a patient is given insulin for diabetes?

options.A: Monitoring for a sudden dangerous drop in blood sugar
options.B: Ensuring the patient's blood pressure does not rise too high
options.C: Assessing the patient for sudden changes in heart rhythm
options.D: Checking the patient for signs of a severe bacterial infection

explanation: Insulin sweeps glucose out of the blood and into cells. If food intake doesn't match, blood sugar can drop dangerously low (hypoglycemia).

question: Why is community engagement important for adolescent health programs?

options.A: It forces all teenagers in the neighborhood to visit the hospital daily
options.B: It gives the nursing staff extra financial bonuses from the local government
options.C: It eliminates the need for any trained medical personnel in the clinic
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term support for sensitive health topics

explanation: Involving community leaders and parents prevents resistance and builds strong local backing for youth programs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h8)

question: What is the main goal of taking and handing over on the ward?

options.A: To transfer patient care responsibilities safely between shifts
options.B: To replace formal written patient medical records completely
options.C: To give nurses a chance to socialise before starting work
options.D: To allow doctors to check if nurses are doing their jobs

explanation: Handover makes sure that important care details move securely from the outgoing nurse to the incoming one, so no patient is left unprotected!

question: What makes friction the most important part of the handwashing process?

options.A: It warms up the water to kill resistant bacterial spores
options.B: It creates bubbles that dry out the skin's outer layer
options.C: It physically removes transient microorganisms from skin surfaces
options.D: It activates the antiseptic chemicals inside standard soap

explanation: The rubbing action of friction is what actually loosens and sweeps away transient germs clinging to the oils on your hands. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order a plain spine X-ray for a patient who just fell?

options.A: To see if the spinal cord is bruised or swollen
options.B: To look for hidden bleeding inside the brain
options.C: To measure how fast nerves carry signals
options.D: To check bone alignment and rule out broken bones

explanation: Spine X-rays give a quick view of bone structure to make sure there are no fractures after a fall.

question: Why is recovery in rehabilitation often described as non-linear or up-and-down?

options.A: Therapists change goals randomly every single day
options.B: Insurance companies dictate how many phases a patient must skip
options.C: Medical staff rarely document patient improvements
options.D: Patients often experience setbacks that require adjusting the care plan

explanation: Healing isn't a straight line! Good days and bad days happen, and nurses adjust care plans to match how the patient is feeling.

question: A nurse is preparing to use a blood pressure cuff on a patient with unbroken skin. How should this item be classified and processed?

options.A: Semi-critical item requiring high-level chemical disinfection
options.B: Critical item requiring high-pressure steam sterilization
options.C: Non-critical item requiring low to intermediate-level disinfection
options.D: Sterile item requiring single-use disposal packaging

explanation: Blood pressure cuffs touch only intact skin, making them non-critical items that only need routine low or intermediate disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: How can severe emotional stress or extreme physical exercise affect a woman's monthly cycle?

options.A: It can mess with brain signals and cause missed periods
options.B: It causes permanent cessation of all body hair
options.C: It doubles the daily production of red blood cells
options.D: It permanently enlarges the uterus

explanation: The brain and hormones are closely linked! High stress or over-exercising can trick the hypothalamus into pausing the hormones needed for regular ovulation.

question: What is a key role of a community health nurse when working alongside NGOs?

options.A: Manufacturing medical vaccines in hospital laboratories
options.B: Acting as a bridge between visiting volunteers and local patients
options.C: Auditing the international bank accounts of donor agencies
options.D: Writing new federal health laws for parliament

explanation: You're right! Nurses connect outside volunteers with local residents, making sure everyone understands each other and gets the best care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h7)

question: How does a global body like the International Council of Nurses (ICN) differ from a local national association?

options.A: The ICN writes the specific nursing school curricula for every country
options.B: The ICN manages local salary disputes for individual clinics
options.C: The ICN directly licenses nurses to work in specific hospitals
options.D: The ICN federates national associations to address global health issues

explanation: While national bodies look at local laws, the ICN brings different countries together to tackle worldwide challenges like nursing shortages and global health policies.

question: What are national food buffer stocks primarily used for?

options.A: To dispose of old crops that failed safety inspections
options.B: To export surplus food for maximum international profit
options.C: To feed military personnel during peacetime training exercises
options.D: To stabilize market prices during shortages or surpluses

explanation: Buffer stocks allow governments to release or store food to control extreme price fluctuations. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nursing team to share their successful hospital study with others?

options.A: Keeping the final report locked inside a private desk drawer
options.B: Presenting at a healthcare conference or publishing in a peer-reviewed journal
options.C: Posting raw data sheets on a public community notice board
options.D: Destroying all copies to protect hospital operational secrets

explanation: Good nursing knowledge is meant to be shared! Conferences and journals help spread great ideas so patient care improves everywhere.

question: Into how many main categories does the World Health Organization divide FGM?

options.A: Six distinct types
options.B: Two distinct types
options.C: Four distinct types
options.D: Three distinct types

explanation: You got it! The WHO classifies FGM into four broad types based on the method and extent of tissue removed.

question: How does a public health nurse help prevent abuse by starting a support group for young, first-time parents?

options.A: By forcing families to report their income to the government
options.B: By replacing the need for pediatric medical check-ups
options.C: By monitoring parents for illegal drug use in their homes
options.D: By building parenting skills and reducing social isolation

explanation: Connecting young parents with peers and teaching them parenting skills stops the loneliness and frustration that can lead to abuse.

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only at home, while quarantine is strictly used inside hospitals.
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts healthy people who were exposed.
options.C: Isolation applies to bacteria, while quarantine applies exclusively to viral infections.
options.D: Isolation requires wearing PPE, while quarantine requires taking chemoprophylaxis.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick with an infection, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait to see if they fall ill.

question: What condition frequently threatens family members who provide ongoing home support?

options.A: Mandatory legal liability for nursing errors
options.B: Chronic hospital-acquired pneumonia from visiting wards
options.C: Caregiver burnout from constant physical and emotional strain
options.D: Sudden loss of personal health insurance coverage

explanation: Managing a sick relative at home without breaks often leads to profound exhaustion and stress for families. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why do we regularly check liver function and platelet counts for a mum with severe preeclampsia?

options.A: To calculate her exact delivery date
options.B: To check for liver stress and HELLP syndrome
options.C: To check if the baby can breathe on its own
options.D: To find out the sex of the baby

explanation: Severe preeclampsia can sneak up on the liver and use up clotting cells (platelets). Watching these lab results helps us catch dangerous changes early!

question: What is one of the most important nursing duties when caring for a patient with a GI disorder?

options.A: Performing independent endoscopy exams
options.B: Tracking exact fluid intake and output
options.C: Diagnosing the primary medical illness
options.D: Prescribing emergency surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! Accurate fluid charts help nurses catch dangerous fluid losses or fluid buildup early when bleeding, vomiting, or diarrhea strike. Essential nursing care!

question: Why is interconception care (care between pregnancies) so important in safe motherhood?

options.A: It improves health and nutrition before the next pregnancy begins
options.B: It only focuses on baby immunizations
options.C: It replaces the need for medical care during pregnancy
options.D: It forces couples to delay having children

explanation: You've got it! Caring for a mother between pregnancies builds up her health, making her stronger and safer before she conceives again.

question: What are the two most common causes of acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Stomach ulcers and low dietary fiber
options.B: Bacterial infection and high salt intake
options.C: Autoimmune disease and heavy smoking
options.D: Gallstones and chronic alcohol abuse

explanation: Gallstones blocking the bile duct and excessive alcohol consumption account for the vast majority of acute pancreatitis cases. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why is nurse coordination so important when a patient is seeing multiple medical specialists?

options.A: To perform advanced surgical procedures in community clinics
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of private specialist consultations
options.C: To replace the need for regular primary healthcare visits
options.D: To prevent conflicting treatment plans and ensure smooth communication

explanation: When too many doctors are involved, advice can clash! As nurses, we bring everything together to keep our patients safe. Brilliant teamwork!

question: What does scientific empiricism primarily rely on for gathering medical knowledge?

options.A: Strict adherence to ancient religious texts
options.B: Careful observation and physical experimentation
options.C: Interpreting dreams and spiritual visions
options.D: Blind trust in traditional folklore

explanation: Empiricism values tangible evidence gained through direct observation, testing, and experimentation rather than accepting claims based on tradition or authority alone. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is a subgaleal hemorrhage considered a life-threatening emergency in a newborn?

options.A: It causes immediate respiratory arrest
options.B: It dissolves the cranial bones completely
options.C: It always results in permanent facial paralysis
options.D: It holds enough blood to cause severe shock

explanation: The large potential space beneath the galea aponeurosis can accumulate a massive amount of blood, leading to rapid hypovolemia and shock. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h3)

question: How can extreme poverty drive some families to practice early marriage?

options.A: By allowing the young bride to immediately secure high-paying employment
options.B: By guaranteeing free government housing for the newly wed couple
options.C: By reducing household financial burdens and sometimes yielding a bride price
options.D: By eliminating all taxes for families with married daughters

explanation: You got it! In severe economic hardship, some families feel pressured to marry off daughters to reduce mouths to feed or to gain financial help from a bride price.

question: When you first rush to help a crashing patient, what is your number one priority (the primary survey)?

options.A: Airway, breathing, circulation, and disability
options.B: Past medical history and family financial status
options.C: Detailed psychological coping mechanisms
options.D: Surgical site aesthetics and dressing color

explanation: Always remember ABCDE! Life-threatening issues come first before anything else. If they can't breathe or their heart isn't pumping right, nothing else matters.

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of secondary prevention in respiratory health?

options.A: Finding small pulmonary nodules on routine diagnostic imaging
options.B: Reversing the genetic mutations that cause inherited lung disorders
options.C: Identifying early airway obstruction using breathing tests
options.D: Catching latent infections before they become active and contagious

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and treatment of existing disease, not genetic modification or primary prevention of DNA mutations. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of leaving faeces in contact with the perineal skin for too long?

options.A: Enzymes and bacteria cause painful skin breakdown and dermatitis
options.B: Hair growth in the pelvic region stops completely
options.C: The skin permanently changes to a darker color
options.D: Subcutaneous fat layers begin to increase

explanation: Faecal enzymes irritate the skin barrier, leading to rapid inflammation, excoriation, and painful breakdown if not cleaned promptly. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h7)

question: How does the schistosomiasis parasite usually get into the human body?

options.A: Skin penetration by cercariae in contaminated water
options.B: Inhalation of airborne dust near infected rivers
options.C: Ingestion of poorly cooked freshwater fish
options.D: Bites from infected mosquitoes near stagnant pools

explanation: The parasite doesn't wait to be swallowed—it swims right through healthy, unbroken skin when someone wades or swims in an infected stream. Keep up the great studying!

question: A conscious patient with terminal cancer firmly refuses a blood transfusion because of personal beliefs. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Administer the blood anyway because it is life-saving
options.B: Ask the family to force the patient to accept the treatment
options.C: Wait until the patient falls asleep and give the transfusion
options.D: Respect the refusal and notify the healthcare team

explanation: Even if treatment can save a life, a competent adult has the legal and ethical right to refuse it. Always honor your patient's autonomy and inform the team!

question: What is a direct result of successfully balancing personal and organisational objectives in a hospital?

options.A: The hospital completely stops admitting emergency patients
options.B: Staff turnover drops because nurses feel valued and supported
options.C: Training costs increase due to constant staff replacements
options.D: All nurses immediately resign to work in other industries

explanation: When nurses feel heard, respected, and supported in achieving their goals, they stay on the job and don't rush to resign!

question: Why is keeping a good stock of uterotonic drugs critical in a PAC unit?

options.A: To prevent or treat severe uterine bleeding and hemorrhage
options.B: To reverse the side effects of general anesthesia
options.C: To speed up the return of normal ovulation cycles
options.D: To relieve severe lower abdominal cramping pain

explanation: Uterotonics like oxytocin or misoprostol make the uterine muscle contract, which is a lifesaver for stopping dangerous blood loss after evacuation.

question: How do teenage boys often express deep emotional stress when society tells them never to show weakness?

options.A: Through anger, substance abuse, and high-risk behaviors
options.B: By asking nurses for frequent mental health checkups
options.C: By openly crying and seeking immediate group counseling
options.D: Through excessive journaling and emotional sharing

explanation: You got it! Since boys are often taught to hide sadness, their internal pain frequently comes out as anger, substance use, or dangerous actions.

question: A patient facing severe financial hardship asks you about family planning. What is her money constraint most likely to affect?

options.A: Her natural immunity against common infections
options.B: Her ability to consistently buy and use modern contraceptives
options.C: Her biological response to hormonal medications
options.D: Her genetic predisposition to chronic illnesses

explanation: That's right! Money worries directly affect purchasing power, making it tough to afford steady supplies of birth control.

question: What is the best next step for a patient who comes back with a strongly positive Mantoux test?

options.A: Discharge the patient with instructions to return next year
options.B: Refer the patient for a chest X-ray and clinical evaluation
options.C: Immediately start a full course of multi-drug TB treatment
options.D: Administer a second booster Mantoux test on the other arm

explanation: A positive skin test is a warning sign, not a final diagnosis. We always send them for a chest X-ray to check if their lungs are clear or if the infection is active. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)

question: What is the main difference between making an infusion and making a decoction?

options.A: Decoctions are always applied topically, while infusions are inhaled
options.B: Infusions use alcohol exclusively, while decoctions use only palm oil
options.C: Decoctions involve boiling hard parts, while infusions soak softer parts
options.D: Infusions require high-pressure machinery, unlike simple decoctions

explanation: Think of it like tea: tough roots and bark need a good long boil (decoction) to release their goodness, while soft leaves just need a gentle soak (infusion).

question: How can emotional stress or anxiety push teenagers toward phone addiction?

options.A: Anxiety directly increases the physical speed at which a person can type
options.B: Screens provide a temporary escape from real-world stress and painful feelings
options.C: Worrying about schoolwork forces them to read more online articles
options.D: Depressed teenagers have higher nutritional needs for computer equipment

explanation: Phones can become a quick way to numb hard feelings. While it brings temporary relief, it stops teens from learning healthy ways to handle stress.

question: During which gestational weeks is screening for gestational diabetes routinely performed in uncomplicated pregnancies?

options.A: 24 to 28 weeks
options.B: 8 to 12 weeks
options.C: 16 to 20 weeks
options.D: 34 to 38 weeks

explanation: Insulin resistance typically peaks during the late second trimester, making 24 to 28 weeks the standard window for gestational diabetes screening. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h4)

question: What minimum level of medication adherence is needed to keep HIV fully suppressed over the long term?

options.A: Around 50%
options.B: Exactly 20%
options.C: At least 95%
options.D: Only on weekends

explanation: You got it! HIV treatment requires consistency. Taking at least 95% of doses on schedule keeps the virus cornered and unable to fight back.

question: Why would a doctor remove a small cervical polyp even if it isn't causing any symptoms?

options.A: To restore normal ovarian function
options.B: To stop potential future bleeding and permit testing
options.C: To prevent the spread of severe bacterial infection
options.D: To enlarge the cervical opening for childbirth

explanation: Taking it out stops random spotting before it starts and lets the lab test the tissue just to be completely safe.

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest number of calories per gram?

options.A: Fat
options.B: Protein
options.C: Water
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Fats are the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying nine kilocalories for every single gram consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: Why do public health workers look beyond the hospital clinic to address community health?

options.A: Government policies prevent nurses from treating patients alone
options.B: Health sectors cannot function without direct financial profits
options.C: Doctors require assistance from construction workers inside the wards
options.D: Factors outside the clinic like housing and sanitation heavily influence health

explanation: Spot on! Good health isn't just about hospital care; clean water, housing, and food play a massive role in keeping people well.

question: Which of the following organs is NOT typically considered a primary target organ damaged by long-term hypertension?

options.A: Brain
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Heart

explanation: The primary target organs damaged by chronic high blood pressure are the heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h7)

question: Which lifestyle change is a major reason diabetes is becoming more common in Nigerian cities?

options.A: Engaging in heavy manual farm labor every morning
options.B: Consuming excessive amounts of natural spring water
options.C: Increasing daily intake of green leafy vegetables
options.D: Adopting processed diets and reducing physical activity

explanation: With busy city life, more people eat fast, processed foods and move around less. This shift in lifestyle greatly increases metabolic risks. Great insight for community nursing!

question: Why do we encourage new mothers to get up and walk around (ambulate) early after childbirth?

options.A: To speed up the immediate closure of the cervix
options.B: To reduce the risk of blood clots and improve circulation
options.C: To encourage the baby to sleep through the night
options.D: To prevent the mother from producing too much colostrum

explanation: Getting moving gets the blood pumping! It keeps circulation strong and stops blood from pooling in the legs, preventing dangerous clots. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: When is a nurse researcher most likely to use a non-directional hypothesis?

options.A: When there is strong evidence supporting an increase
options.B: When the statistical software requires a one-tailed test
options.C: When little previous research exists on the topic
options.D: When the null hypothesis has already been proven true

explanation: If no one has studied the topic much before, you might not know which way things will go, so you keep it non-directional.

question: What is the common name for exercises designed to strengthen the pelvic floor muscles?

options.A: Aerobic exercises
options.B: Range of motion drills
options.C: Kegel exercises
options.D: Isometric stretches

explanation: Kegel exercises involve repeatedly contracting and relaxing the pelvic floor muscles to improve structural support and urinary control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: What goes on inside a resting heart cell (polarized state)?

options.A: Electrical charges stop moving entirely throughout the whole body
options.B: The inside of the cell maintains a negative electrical charge
options.C: The cell membrane completely dissolves to release stored energy
options.D: Positive ions continuously rush inward to keep the heart pumping

explanation: When resting, the inside of the cell stays cozy and negative compared to the outside, waiting for the next signal.

question: You notice a surgeon accidentally touches their non-sterile mask with a gloved hand during a procedure. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Politely inform the surgeon of the break in technique and ensure the gloves are changed
options.B: Assume the gloves are still clean because the mask was recently put on
options.C: Ask the circulating nurse to document the event in the patient's chart
options.D: Wait until the end of the operation to mention the incident to the head nurse

explanation: Patient safety is everyone's job. Speak up kindly and immediately if sterility is broken so the team can fix it right away!

question: What was the main operational breakthrough that led to the creation of the first formal ICU?

options.A: Centralizing critically ill patients and specialized breathing support in one location
options.B: Discovering broad-spectrum antibiotics to cure bacterial infections
options.C: Developing advanced surgical techniques for open-heart operations
options.D: Inventing the first computerized electronic health record system

explanation: Grouping unstable patients together allowed specialized staff to use newly invented ventilation techniques more efficiently. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why are males more commonly affected by X-linked recessive disorders than females?

options.A: The Y chromosome protects female offspring
options.B: Males possess only one X chromosome
options.C: X chromosomes only exist in male bodies
options.D: Females do not have any chromosomes

explanation: Since males only have one X chromosome, a single recessive mutation on that chromosome will express the disease, whereas females have a backup X chromosome. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h2)

question: A visitor bumps the bed and a weight bag touches the floor. What is your very first step?

options.A: Immediately remove the skull pins to prevent further injury
options.B: Document the incident and wait for the doctor's morning round
options.C: Call the physical therapist to readjust the entire bed frame
options.D: Ensure the rope is in the pulley and lift the weight so it hangs freely

explanation: Quick action is key! Just check the rope and make sure those weights are hanging freely again to keep the traction working.

question: Why is patient education a powerful nursing tool against under-prescription?

options.A: It ensures patients refuse all medications to save money
options.B: It empowers patients to ask their doctors about standard therapies for their illness
options.C: It prevents doctors from making any clinical errors during visits
options.D: It teaches patients how to fill their own prescriptions at the pharmacy

explanation: Knowledge is power! When patients understand what treatments are standard for their condition, they can speak up and ask if their care plan includes them.

question: You are preparing a recovery bed for a patient coming back from theatre. Which item must you keep ready at the bedside?

options.A: An overhead exercise trapeze bar
options.B: Suction apparatus and emesis basin
options.C: Bedside dining tray and reading lamp
options.D: A heavy woolen floor rug and extra pillows

explanation: Great job! Patients waking up from anesthesia can easily choke on saliva or vomit, so having a suction machine and a basin nearby is a lifesaver.

question: Why is establishing a baseline neurological assessment important for a patient?

options.A: It eliminates the need for vital sign monitoring
options.B: It gives a starting point to track future changes in status
options.C: It completely prevents any future neurological complications
options.D: It determines the patient's exact date of hospital discharge

explanation: Having a clear baseline allows the healthcare team to notice early signs of improvement or deterioration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is the eardrum (tympanic membrane) such a great spot to check core body temperature?

options.A: It shares a blood supply with the brain's temperature center
options.B: It is completely protected from any room air
options.C: Earwax never affects the reading
options.D: It always shows the highest temperature on the body

explanation: The eardrum shares blood vessels with the hypothalamus (your body's thermostat), giving you a very true picture of core temperature.

question: Where does the circulating nurse work during a surgical procedure?

options.A: Outside the sterile field, managing room coordination and documentation
options.B: Inside the sterile field, handling surgical instruments directly
options.C: In the hospital pharmacy preparing medications
options.D: In the recovery ward away from the surgical suite

explanation: Well done! The circulating nurse stays unscrubbed and moves around outside the sterile zone to coordinate and handle records.

question: A patient comes in with right upper quadrant belly pain, fever, and a history of dysentery. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: A perforated stomach ulcer
options.B: An amoebic liver abscess
options.C: Acute appendicitis
options.D: Severe kidney stones

explanation: Spot on! When the parasites travel up into the liver via the bloodstream, they can form a painful, pus-filled abscess.

question: Which physical sign might make a nurse suspect that an outpatient has anemia?

options.A: Swollen finger joints
options.B: Yellowing of the teeth
options.C: Pale conjunctiva
options.D: Excessive hair growth

explanation: You're doing great! Checking the inner eyelids (conjunctiva) for paleness is a quick way to spot low red blood cells or iron deficiency.

question: Why is it risky for a nursing research project to lack clear objectives?

options.A: The study will easily lose direction and gather irrelevant data
options.B: The nursing staff will refuse to participate in the study
options.C: The sample size will become too large to calculate
options.D: The hospital ethics committee will automatically grant funding

explanation: Without clear targets, you might end up collecting a mountain of unnecessary information that doesn't actually solve your clinical problem. Good objectives keep you focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is the standard defaulter rate commonly measured in routine immunization programs?

options.A: The drop-out rate between the first and last doses of a series
options.B: The percentage of expired vaccine vials found in the fridge
options.C: The total number of babies born in a hospital annually
options.D: The daily count of pregnant women attending antenatal care

explanation: The drop-out rate—such as the difference between Penta 1 and Penta 3 uptake—is the standard metric used to measure defaulting. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h6)

question: What is the best way to tell if a food safety training program actually worked?

options.A: Watching to see if workers practice safe habits on the kitchen floor
options.B: Making sure everyone memorized the manual word-for-word
options.C: Calculating how much money was spent on the workshop
options.D: Checking that everyone sat through every minute of the lecture

explanation: Real learning shows in daily habits! True success is when staff actually use what they learned while cooking and cleaning.

question: A newborn delivered after a prolonged labor with severe cephalopelvic disproportion is at the highest risk for which condition?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.B: Neural tube closure failure
options.C: Congenital heart defect
options.D: Foetal skull injury

explanation: Prolonged pressure against a tight pelvis creates intense mechanical stress, making the infant very vulnerable to cranial trauma. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h2)

question: Which group of substances includes alcohol and benzodiazepines?

options.A: Depressants
options.B: Hallucinogens
options.C: Stimulants
options.D: Cannabinoids

explanation: Depressants slow down central nervous system activity, lowering heart rate, blood pressure, and breathing. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has long-term high blood pressure and is carrying twins. What should you, as her nurse, watch out for?

options.A: She has zero risk of complications because she is young.
options.B: She should stop all her blood pressure tablets right away.
options.C: She only needs normal, routine antenatal visits.
options.D: She needs closer monitoring for early signs of preeclampsia.

explanation: Having twins plus chronic high blood pressure puts her at a higher risk, so we need to keep a closer, caring eye on her throughout her pregnancy.

question: Why is every single link in the chain of infection important for a disease to spread?

options.A: Germs require all links simultaneously to grow larger
options.B: The host becomes immune if a link is missing
options.C: Pathogens cannot survive outside the reservoir link
options.D: Breaking any single link stops the cycle of infection

explanation: Think of it like a chain: if you break just one link, the infection cannot travel further. That is why simple actions like handwashing are so powerful!

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Use barrier methods consistently to help prevent reinfection.
options.B: Make sure your sexual partner is treated at the same time.
options.C: Stop taking your medicine as soon as the discharge lessens.
options.D: Avoid having sex until your treatment is fully completed.

explanation: Never advise stopping meds early just because symptoms fade. They must finish the entire course!

question: What is the main goal of a subacute care facility?

options.A: Treating minor outpatient ailments and routine infections
options.B: Managing acute life-threatening surgical emergencies
options.C: Providing short-term rehabilitation and medical management
options.D: Offering permanent residential care for healthy elders

explanation: Spot on! Subacute care bridges the gap between the busy hospital ward and home, giving patients targeted rehab and recovery support.

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.C: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: You got it! Keeping vaccines between +2°C and +8°C keeps them fresh and effective without freezing them by accident.

question: Why are professional nursing organizations important for your everyday life as a nurse?

options.A: They supply all consumable medical equipment to hospitals
options.B: They establish practice standards and shape health policies
options.C: They dictate the exact daily schedule of ward nurses
options.D: They manage direct disciplinary action for individual negligence

explanation: Think of these organizations as the voice of the profession. By creating guidelines and advocating for better policies, they help ensure safe, high-quality patient care everywhere.

question: What is the main purpose of adding PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure) to a ventilator?

options.A: To keep tiny air sacs in the lungs from collapsing at the end of exhalation
options.B: To force carbon dioxide out of the bloodstream into the lungs faster
options.C: To prevent the patient from waking up during sedation holidays
options.D: To measure the exact strength of the patient's heart contractions

explanation: PEEP acts like a gentle push that keeps the tiny lung air sacs open, making it much easier for the patient to absorb oxygen.

question: Which blood marker is commonly measured to help screen for prostate disorders?

options.A: Plasma glucose
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Serum creatinine
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen

explanation: Elevated levels of prostate-specific antigen can indicate inflammation, enlargement, or cancer within the prostate. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why do we use synthetic swab tips (like dacron) instead of regular cotton?

options.A: Synthetic swabs change color to indicate a positive infection
options.B: Cotton can inhibit certain laboratory tests and microbial growth
options.C: Synthetic tips are significantly cheaper to purchase in bulk
options.D: Cotton fibers dissolve completely when exposed to body fluids

explanation: Regular cotton can actually trap or stop germs from growing properly in the lab, so synthetic swabs give us much more reliable test results.

question: Why must nurses understand basic inventory and stock control principles?

options.A: To design new storage shelves for the hospital
options.B: To negotiate better prices with medical suppliers
options.C: To take over the job of the hospital pharmacist
options.D: To prevent emergency supply shortages on the ward

explanation: Nurses handle ward supplies every day, so knowing stock rules helps them prevent running out of critical items during patient care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: What is the big advantage of modern low-osmolality ORS compared to the older, stronger formula?

options.A: It reduces stool volume and the need for IV fluids
options.B: It provides all the daily vitamins a growing child needs
options.C: It tastes much sweeter and dissolves instantly in cold water
options.D: It cures bacterial infections without needing antibiotics

explanation: By lowering the sugar and salt slightly, the modern formula creates less osmotic pull in the gut, which means less watery stool and fewer trips to the hospital for drips!

question: How can you, as a bedside nurse, help improve injection safety standards in your clinic?

options.A: By buying new safety syringes with your own personal money
options.B: By reporting unsafe practices and joining safety audits
options.C: By handling all medical waste disposal completely alone
options.D: By refusing to give any injections during night shifts

explanation: Well done! Speaking up about risks and taking part in safety checks helps fix system flaws and protects everyone. You're thinking like a professional nurse! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: A widow of eight months says daily that she wishes she were dead to join her husband and won't leave her house. What should you do?

options.A: Reassure her that wanting to join her husband is completely normal
options.B: Refer the patient for immediate mental health evaluation and counseling
options.C: Advise her to take up a new hobby to distract her mind from sadness
options.D: Wait another four months before taking any clinical action

explanation: Safety first! Talk of wanting to die combined with severe withdrawal means the patient needs immediate professional mental health support.

question: What usually stops teenagers from visiting clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory free distribution of supplies in schools
options.B: A complete absence of hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Fear of being judged and a lack of privacy from staff
options.D: Strict laws requiring adolescent doctors for teenage patients

explanation: Teens often avoid seeking help because they are scared healthcare workers will gossip, judge them, or break their trust. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: A patient experiences a sudden seizure that immediately affects both sides of the brain with a total loss of consciousness. How is this classified?

options.A: Peripheral nerve spasm
options.B: Generalized onset seizure
options.C: Localized partial seizure
options.D: Focal aware seizure

explanation: When both brain hemispheres are engaged from the very beginning, the event is classified as a generalized onset seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h3)

question: What should the nurse instruct the patient to do immediately before actuating a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: Inhale as fast as possible through the nose
options.B: Hyperventilate for thirty seconds
options.C: Exhale completely to empty the lungs
options.D: Take a quick swallow of cold water

explanation: Exhaling fully clears space in the lungs so the subsequent slow, deep inhalation can pull maximum medication into the airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: How do unsterile injection techniques lead to painful abscesses?

options.A: By introducing bacteria from the skin surface deep into the muscle tissue
options.B: By causing an immediate chemical reaction that dissolves bone tissue
options.C: By increasing the local blood flow until the tissue swells and bursts
options.D: By freezing the surrounding muscle fibers and destroying blood vessels

explanation: When germs are pushed past the skin into warm muscle, they multiply, cause inflammation, and form pus (an abscess). Good antisepsis stops this!

question: A patient is breathing rapidly at 34 breaths per minute and straining their neck muscles to breathe. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the findings as normal vital signs for an adult and schedule a routine follow-up
options.B: Recognize this as severe respiratory distress and prepare immediate oxygen and triage support
options.C: Advise the patient to lie flat on their back and sleep off the exhaustion
options.D: Administer an oral antipyretic medication for presumed fever

explanation: Using accessory neck muscles and breathing super fast are clear SOS signs of severe breathing trouble. Time to act fast with oxygen!

question: What is the medical term for dangerously high blood sugar?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Hypokalemia
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Hyperglycemia just means too much glucose floating in the blood. You've got this! Keep building that nursing vocabulary.

question: A nurse fills out a Yellow Form for a patient who got a rash after taking two new drugs and an herbal supplement. What should be included in the medication history?

options.A: Only document the drug that the nurse personally administered
options.B: List all prescribed drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products
options.C: Ignore the herbal supplement since it is not a pharmaceutical drug
options.D: Only list the most expensive brand-name prescription drug

explanation: Always list everything! Herbal remedies and over-the-counter items frequently cause or contribute to adverse reactions.

question: During early development, which main germ layer gives rise to all of our muscle tissues?

options.A: Blastoderm
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: You've got this! The middle germ layer, the mesoderm, is responsible for building our skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles. Think 'M for middle and muscle!'

question: When is an employer usually NOT held liable for a nurse's action?

options.A: When the nurse engages in a major personal detour from work duties
options.B: When the nurse follows a hospital protocol that contains a minor flaw
options.C: When the nurse makes a standard medication calculation error on the ward
options.D: When the nurse takes a short authorized break inside the hospital building

explanation: If you leave your post to go handle a major personal errand far away, you've stepped outside your job description, and the hospital is off the hook for what happens.

question: How does the work differ between a Senior CHEW and a Junior CHEW?

options.A: Junior CHEWs perform major surgeries, while Seniors only do paperwork
options.B: Senior CHEWs only work in cities, while Juniors work exclusively abroad
options.C: Senior CHEWs handle independent diagnoses and treatments under protocol, while Juniors work under closer supervision
options.D: There is no difference in their training or daily clinical duties

explanation: You got it! Senior CHEWs have extra training that lets them manage common health issues independently using standing orders, while juniors work more closely with supervisors.

question: What is the term for the natural home where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: A transmission route
options.B: A reservoir
options.C: A susceptible host
options.D: A portal of exit

explanation: A reservoir acts as the primary habitat where microorganisms thrive and multiply before infecting a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is a major focus of donor-supported family planning programs in primary health clinics?

options.A: Mandating contraceptive use for all married couples
options.B: Building private hospitals in every rural community
options.C: Replacing all local doctors with foreign medical experts
options.D: Preventing commodity stock-outs and training health staff

explanation: These programs focus heavily on making sure clinics never run out of supplies and helping local healthcare workers build their clinical skills.

question: What is the primary job of the protein dystrophin in healthy skeletal muscle?

options.A: Transporting calcium ions out of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.B: Generating the electrical action potential along the sarcolemma
options.C: Linking the muscle cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix
options.D: Acting as the primary enzyme that breaks down glucose for energy

explanation: Dystrophin acts like a sturdy internal anchor, connecting the muscle cell's inner framework to its outer environment for stability during contractions.

question: Which setting is best for an older adult who needs round-the-clock nursing checks and complex wound care?

options.A: Assisted living facility
options.B: Skilled nursing facility
options.C: Independent living apartment
options.D: Continuing care retirement community

explanation: Great thinking! A skilled nursing facility provides the 24/7 professional nursing oversight needed for heavy clinical tasks like complex wound care.

question: What role do prostaglandins play when someone develops a fever?

options.A: They attack and destroy bacteria in the blood
options.B: They relax muscles to stop shivering
options.C: They turn on sweat glands to cool the skin
options.D: They tell the hypothalamus to raise the body's temperature setting

explanation: You're doing great! Prostaglandins act like messengers telling your brain's thermostat to crank up the heat.

question: What is the main risk of aggressively stripping surgical drainage tubes?

options.A: It can create a strong vacuum that damages delicate internal tissue
options.B: It always causes the collection container to crack and leak fluid
options.C: It permanently ruins the plastic so it can no longer collect blood
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling any post-operative surgical pain

explanation: Stripping generates high negative pressure inside the tube, which can suck delicate tissue into the drainage holes and cause injury or bleeding. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: How does the growing baby and uterus contribute to constipation later in pregnancy?

options.A: By increasing the production of digestive enzymes
options.B: By putting direct mechanical pressure on the bowels
options.C: By completely stopping the production of stomach acid
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the colon

explanation: Exactly! As the baby grows, there is less space in the tummy, and the heavy uterus presses right against the intestines, slowing things down.

question: Why is family planning considered a key pillar of safe motherhood?

options.A: It helps women space pregnancies to protect their physical health
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.C: It completely stops women from experiencing menopause
options.D: It guarantees that every baby born will be a male child

explanation: Giving mum's body time to rest and rebuild strength between babies means a healthier mother and a safer next pregnancy!

question: What is the primary purpose of involving physical therapists in the care of a patient with a mobility impairment?

options.A: To design safe mobility plans and select appropriate assistive devices
options.B: To cook specialized nutritional meals for rehabilitation
options.C: To perform daily hygiene and bathing tasks for the patient
options.D: To prescribe routine medications for chronic neuropathic pain

explanation: Physical therapists specialize in restoring and maintaining movement, making them vital partners in choosing mobility aids and creating exercise regimens. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which medication is commonly given long-term to help prevent future gout attacks by lowering uric acid production?

options.A: Allopurinol
options.B: Colchicine
options.C: Prednisone
options.D: Ibuprofen

explanation: Spot on! Allopurinol is a daily helper that blocks the body's enzyme from making too much uric acid in the first place.

question: What is the primary danger of delaying stock card updates until the end of the week?

options.A: Hospital management will reduce the overall budget of the nursing unit
options.B: The central store will automatically double the next order quantity
options.C: Arithmetic errors and forgotten items lead to inaccurate stock balances
options.D: The medications on the shelf will automatically change their expiry dates

explanation: Relying on memory hours or days later results in guessing quantities, which destroys the reliability of the inventory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which of these common items spoils easily if left outside the fridge in warm weather?

options.A: Dry white rice
options.B: Canned tomato paste
options.C: Granulated sugar
options.D: Fresh milk

explanation: Correct! Fresh milk has plenty of moisture and nutrients, making it a playground for bacteria if left unchilled.

question: During an IV insertion, what lets you know for sure that your needle has successfully entered the vein?

options.A: The infusion bag begins to drip rapidly without any pressure.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cool to the touch.
options.C: The patient reports a sudden cooling sensation in the arm.
options.D: A flash of blood appears inside the flashback chamber of the device.

explanation: That's right! Seeing that little 'flash' of dark red blood in the chamber is the classic sign that you're in the vein. Beautiful work!

question: What is the main reason for doing a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To test physical strength for office roles
options.B: To determine retirement pension packages
options.C: To provide immediate treatment for interview injuries
options.D: To establish a baseline health status before a worker begins a job

explanation: Correct! Pre-placement exams give you a clear starting point of the worker's health so you can notice if the job affects them later.

question: What is the main difference between hypertensive urgency and a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Whether the patient is male or female
options.B: The time of day the blood pressure was checked
options.C: The exact numerical value of the diastolic reading
options.D: The presence of acute target organ damage

explanation: Urgency means extremely high pressure, but emergency means the high pressure is actively harming vital organs like the heart or brain. Big difference in how fast we act!

question: What is the main job of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the surgical wound layers with sutures and staples
options.B: Managing the unsterile environment and monitoring patient safety
options.C: Performing the surgical incisions alongside the primary surgeon
options.D: Administering the general anesthetic gases to the patient

explanation: While the scrub nurse is sterile at the table, the circulating nurse moves freely around the room to coordinate supplies, record notes, and watch out for the patient's safety.

question: What is the primary difference between a hospital-based midwife and a community midwife?

options.A: Hospital midwives work exclusively in private clinics.
options.B: Hospital midwives do not handle deliveries.
options.C: Community midwives actively reach out to rural populations.
options.D: Community midwives only provide postnatal care.

explanation: Community midwifery is defined by its outreach nature, bringing care directly to underserved grassroots populations rather than waiting in a central hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h1)

question: When you get a cut, your body triggers blood clotting where each step activates even more clotting. What kind of loop is this?

options.A: Negative feedback
options.B: Adaptive atrophy
options.C: Homeostatic breakdown
options.D: Positive feedback

explanation: Spot on! Positive feedback pushes a process forward until a goal is reached—like forming a solid clot to stop bleeding before it slows down.

question: A patient just ate a heavy meal loaded with carbs. What happens right away?

options.A: The parathyroid will secrete parathyroid hormone due to calcium shifts
options.B: The adrenal cortex will stop producing cortisol entirely
options.C: The pancreas will release insulin due to rising blood glucose
options.D: The hypothalamus will block all tropic hormone production

explanation: As sugar rises in the blood after eating, the pancreas senses it directly and releases insulin to bring it back down. Simple and smart!

question: Why is home-based curative care important for patients with chronic conditions in rural communities?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any prescription medications
options.B: It allows the nurse to perform complex major surgical operations safely
options.C: It ensures the patient no longer requires follow-up checks at the clinic
options.D: It provides continuous treatment monitoring and reduces frequent hospital visits

explanation: Managing chronic illnesses at home helps patients stick to their treatment plans without traveling long distances to crowded hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h4)

question: What usually causes an infection control unit to launch an outbreak investigation?

options.A: A routine inspection of the hospital kitchen by local police
options.B: An unusual spike in infection numbers above the normal baseline
options.C: The purchase of new computers for the nursing station
options.D: The arrival of a single patient with a common seasonal cold

explanation: Correct! An outbreak is called when infections suddenly happen much more often than usual in a specific area.

question: What is the main goal of the science of improvement in healthcare?

options.A: Reducing hospital operational costs by cutting nursing staff numbers
options.B: Punishing staff members who make medication administration errors
options.C: Discovering entirely new medical treatments through laboratory trials
options.D: Applying proven knowledge to reliably improve daily care processes

explanation: Improvement science simply means taking what we already know works and finding practical, everyday ways to use it consistently in the ward. You've got this!

question: Where do you usually find the cell bodies of most sensory neurons?

options.A: Skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Dorsal root ganglia
options.C: Motor cortex of the brain
options.D: Anterior horns of the spinal cord

explanation: Well done! Sensory neuron cell bodies neatly cluster together in little swellings called dorsal root ganglia right outside the spinal cord.

question: What do we call the natural home where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Reservoir
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Portal of entry

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the home sweet home for germs! It's where they hang out, multiply, and get ready before moving on to a new host.

question: Why is it so important to keep interruptions in chest compressions to a bare minimum when using an AED?

options.A: The AED machine will shut down if compressions continue too long
options.B: Stopping compressions lowers blood flow to the brain and heart
options.C: Pausing compressions causes the AED pads to lose their sticky adhesive
options.D: Continuous motion prevents the AED from detecting breathing sounds

explanation: Every second you pause compressions, blood pressure drops and the brain loses vital oxygen. Keep your hands on the chest as much as possible!

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized factor that influences a patient's ability to adapt to an illness?

options.A: Past life experiences and trauma
options.B: The hospital's interior wall color
options.C: Cultural beliefs regarding health
options.D: Available social and family support

explanation: Internal and external factors like culture, support systems, and personal history deeply affect adaptation, whereas minor environmental aesthetics do not dictate coping capacity. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h4)

question: Your clinical instructor praises you in front of the ward for a clean hand hygiene routine. What concept is this?

options.A: Extinction protocol
options.B: Negative reinforcement
options.C: Positive reinforcement
options.D: Constructivist scaffolding

explanation: Well done! Giving praise adds a feel-good reward right after a great action, making you much more likely to repeat it next time.

question: How do airborne germs mainly travel from one person to another?

options.A: Through direct contact with contaminated wound dressings
options.B: Through drinking unboiled water from hospital taps
options.C: Through tiny respiratory droplets suspended in the air
options.D: Through sharing unwashed eating utensils at the nurses station

explanation: Airborne pathogens hitch a ride on microscopic moisture droplets that float in the air and can be breathed in by anyone nearby.
