question: What is the main job of an antidote in the body?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of food in the stomach
options.B: To counteract, neutralize, or reverse the effects of a poison
options.C: To stimulate the immune system to fight bacterial infections
options.D: To replace lost blood volume after heavy bleeding

explanation: Spot on! An antidote is specifically crafted to fight back against a toxic substance and turn down its harmful effects in the body.

question: What is one limitation of the placenta's protective barrier role against harmful substances?

options.A: It prevents the passage of essential hormones needed for growth
options.B: Many drugs and viral pathogens can still cross and harm the fetus
options.C: It destroys all maternal antibodies before they reach the fetus
options.D: It completely blocks all medications taken by the mother

explanation: While the placenta filters some toxins, it is not foolproof and allows many drugs, alcohol, and infections to pass through to the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h7)

question: Which sign clearly points to a worsening wound infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the edge of the tape
options.B: Firm, pink tissue filling the wound base
options.C: Foul-smelling, purulent drainage and spreading redness
options.D: A thin layer of clear, watery fluid on the surface

explanation: Pus, a bad smell, and redness that creeps outward are classic red flags that bacteria are taking over and causing an active infection.

question: Which common anti-TB drug is famous for turning urine and tears a harmless red-orange color?

options.A: Ethambutol
options.B: Isoniazid
options.C: Pyrazinamide
options.D: Rifampicin

explanation: Rifampicin gives body fluids a reddish tint. As a nurse, warning your patients about this beforehand saves them a lot of panic!

question: Why don't people usually have severe allergic reactions the very first time they meet a new trigger?

options.A: The body needs time to first build up and sensitize IgE antibodies to that trigger.
options.B: Allergens can only enter the bloodstream after the skin has been damaged twice.
options.C: The immune system is completely dormant until the third or fourth exposure occurs.
options.D: First exposures are always destroyed completely by normal white blood cells in the liver.

explanation: You got it! The first exposure acts as a rehearsal—it primes your immune system by creating those special IgE antibodies, which then react fiercely the *next* time you meet the trigger.

question: A patient has a BMI of 32.5. How is this classified?

options.A: Normal weight
options.B: Overweight
options.C: Obesity
options.D: Underweight

explanation: Any BMI value of 30.0 or higher falls under the classification of obesity. Great clinical recall!

question: What is a major plus for local farmers when they use short food supply chains?

options.A: They earn fairer wages by cutting out intermediaries
options.B: They no longer have to harvest their own vegetables
options.C: They rely on international shipping companies to sell crops
options.D: They are forced to sell their products at a massive loss

explanation: Spot on! By removing middlemen and brokers, farmers get to keep a much fairer share of the profit from their sweat and hard work.

question: What is the primary purpose of using orthopedic traction?

options.A: To apply a pulling force to align bones and reduce spasms
options.B: To completely immobilize the patient without using any bed sheets
options.C: To permanently replace damaged joint cartilage without surgery
options.D: To deliver strong local pain medication directly into a fracture

explanation: Traction uses a steady pull on body parts to restore bone alignment, stretch tight muscles, and ease painful spasms before definitive repair. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of the fimbriae (the finger-like ends of the fallopian tube)?

options.A: To produce progesterone to maintain early pregnancy
options.B: To nourish the sperm during capacitation
options.C: To catch the released oocyte from the ovary
options.D: To block ascending bacterial infections

explanation: Think of the fimbriae as little fingers that gently sweep over the ovary to catch the egg as soon as it's released during ovulation!

question: Which skin layer is found only in thick areas like the palms of your hands and soles of your feet?

options.A: Stratum basale
options.B: Stratum spinosum
options.C: Stratum lucidum
options.D: Stratum corneum

explanation: Spot on! The stratum lucidum is a clear, extra protective layer found only where we experience heavy friction, like our palms and soles.

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in primary health care?

options.A: Empowering locals to take charge of health
options.B: Replacing traditional healers with doctors
options.C: Relying entirely on government funding
options.D: Imposing foreign medical standards

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health problems. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h1)

question: A patient is having a severe panic attack, breathing fast, and crying out in fear. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Hand the patient a stack of educational pamphlets about panic disorder.
options.B: Stay with the patient and speak in calm, short sentences while guiding their breathing.
options.C: Speak loudly and rapidly to snap the patient out of their panic state.
options.D: Leave the room immediately to give the patient privacy to calm down.

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Your calm presence and steady, simple guidance help anchor a patient when their world feels like it's crashing down.

question: What is the largest and least compressible part of the foetal body during birth?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The trunk
options.C: The head
options.D: The pelvis

explanation: The foetal skull is the largest part of the infant body and requires careful passage through the pelvis during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary benefit of a spinal reflex bypassing the brain?

options.A: It stops sensory signals from reaching the skin
options.B: It allows a person to consciously choose how to respond
options.C: It stores long-term memories of painful events
options.D: It allows for much faster reaction times to protect the body

explanation: By bypassing conscious processing in the brain, spinal reflexes can trigger an immediate motor response to prevent injury. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h1)

question: Why is taking a thorough work history so crucial when diagnosing respiratory problems?

options.A: Many lung diseases take years to develop and link directly to past job exposures
options.B: Work history determines the exact blood type of the individual
options.C: Doctors are legally required to record the patient's salary level
options.D: It helps prove whether the patient has a contagious viral infection

explanation: Because symptoms often appear long after the actual dust exposure occurred, a detailed job history is the key to identifying the root cause. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: In family planning, what do we mean by 'typical use' of a birth control method?

options.A: How effectively the method works during everyday, real-life use
options.B: The percentage of people who choose the method on their first visit
options.C: How well the method works when applied correctly every single time
options.D: The laboratory score assigned by the manufacturing pharmaceutical company

explanation: Spot on! 'Typical use' accounts for real life—meaning human errors, busy schedules, or slip-ups that happen outside a lab.

question: Why do doctors order blood tests such as ESR or CRP when evaluating a client with joint pain?

options.A: To rule out inflammatory arthritis or other systemic conditions
options.B: To measure the exact amount of cartilage left inside the knee
options.C: To check if the client has an active vitamin D deficiency
options.D: To track how fast the bone spurs are growing every month

explanation: Because osteoarthritis does not raise inflammatory blood markers, normal blood tests help rule out other forms of arthritis like rheumatoid disease. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: How do checklists help prevent unfair or biased observations in a study?

options.A: By allowing the researcher to change the questions daily
options.B: By evaluating every participant using the same criteria
options.C: By removing human judgment completely from the process
options.D: By hiding the study goals from the clinical staff

explanation: When everyone is measured against the exact same standard, personal opinions won't sway your results. Fair and square!

question: How long should a nurse stay right by the patient's side after a blood transfusion starts?

options.A: Only until the pump is turned on
options.B: The first 15 minutes
options.C: Until the entire bag is empty
options.D: The first two hours

explanation: Most serious transfusion reactions happen fast at the very beginning. Staying close for those first 15 minutes lets you catch and treat any reaction early!

question: Which of these actions should a nurse NOT take when dealing with unhelpful illness behaviour?

options.A: Listen actively to the patient's underlying fears
options.B: Argue aggressively to prove the patient is completely wrong
options.C: Involve medical social workers for holistic support
options.D: Provide clear and simple education about warning signs

explanation: Arguing never works in nursing! It breaks trust and spikes anxiety. We guide with empathy and gentle education instead.

question: Who has the primary legal duty to provide a safe working environment in a hospital?

options.A: The pharmaceutical companies supplying hospital medications
options.B: The individual nursing students on clinical placement
options.C: The patients admitted to the medical and surgical wards
options.D: The hospital management and institutional administration

explanation: Management is legally required to give you safe facilities, working gear, and proper protection so you can do your job without undue risk.

question: What is your very first nursing action if an abdominal wound suddenly pops open and organs are exposed?

options.A: Cover the organs with sterile saline-soaked dressings and call the surgeon.
options.B: Use your gloved fingers to push the organs back inside.
options.C: Wrap a tight binder around the belly to squeeze the organs back in.
options.D: Leave the wound completely open to the fresh air.

explanation: Keep those exposed organs moist with sterile saline gauze so they don't dry out while you call for emergency surgical help. Emergency handled like a champ!

question: Why do daily wage earners find it difficult to attend primary healthcare clinics during the day?

options.A: Clinics refuse to treat people who work in the informal sector
options.B: Transportation is completely unavailable during daytime hours
options.C: Doctors only consult patients during the night
options.D: They lose a day of critical income while waiting at the hospital

explanation: Long daytime waiting hours present a direct financial penalty for men who depend on daily wages to survive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: What is a common result of low health literacy when it comes to family planning?

options.A: Immediate adoption of modern birth control methods
options.B: Increased funding for community health education
options.C: Spread of myths and misconceptions about contraception
options.D: Better understanding of pregnancy danger signs

explanation: When health information is scarce or hard to understand, false stories and rumors easily take over. This is why our patient education role is so vital! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why does a community nurse look at the whole household instead of just one sick person?

options.A: Diseases always hit every family member at the exact same second
options.B: National insurance only pays for whole households
options.C: Hospital rules ban treating single patients alone
options.D: Family members share the same living conditions, risks, and environment

explanation: Brilliant! Since family members eat from the same pot and live under the same roof, a health risk or crisis usually affects everyone in the home.

question: A health team has money to tackle only one issue. They choose malaria because it kills more children in the village than any other disease. Which prioritization criterion are they using?

options.A: Severity and magnitude
options.B: Political interference
options.C: Staff convenience
options.D: Aesthetics and comfort

explanation: Choosing a problem because it affects many people (magnitude) and causes death (severity) is the core of healthcare prioritization. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h5)

question: An 85-year-old retired civil servant comes to the clinic with joint pain and feeling very lonely. Which government program can help with both issues?

options.A: Giving them a heavy-duty vehicle driving license
options.B: Enrolling them in mandatory military training
options.C: Sending them to a full-time industrial workshop
options.D: Geriatric care integration and social protection programs

explanation: Great choice! Specialized geriatric care treats their physical aches, while social programs step in to beat loneliness and build community connection.

question: A woman is pushing very fast with a large baby facing upward and backward. What is she most at risk for?

options.A: Premature rupture of membranes
options.B: Severe perineal laceration
options.C: Hypertensive crisis
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage from atony

explanation: Fast pushing combined with a larger baby and a tricky position puts extra stress on the tissues, greatly increasing the chance of a deep tear.

question: Which sign points strongly to a wound infection after a skin biopsy?

options.A: A thin line of pink tissue along the suture line
options.B: Temporary numbness fading after the local anesthetic wears off
options.C: Spreading redness, warmth, and purulent drainage
options.D: Mild itching around the edges of the adhesive bandage

explanation: Redness that keeps spreading, feeling hot to the touch, pus (purulent drainage), and worsening pain are classic red flags that bacteria have moved in.

question: What simple self-care step should a nurse teach a patient with a mild vulval cyst?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the bare skin for hours
options.B: Wearing tight synthetic underwear to press the swelling down
options.C: Taking warm sitz baths a few times a day
options.D: Scrubbing the area daily with a firm nylon sponge

explanation: Warm sitz baths are wonderful! They ease the tenderness in that sensitive area and can help small cysts drain naturally.

question: What is the main purpose of a healthcare power of attorney document?

options.A: To outline specific funeral arrangements and burial wishes
options.B: To give the nurse permission to administer pain medication
options.C: To designate someone to make medical decisions if the patient becomes incapacitated
options.D: To manage the patient's bank accounts and financial investments

explanation: This document names a trusted person to speak up and make medical choices for the patient when they can no longer speak for themselves. You're nailing these legal concepts!

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose an observational checklist instead of a patient questionnaire?

options.A: Patients prefer being watched over writing answers
options.B: What people say they do can differ from their actual actions
options.C: Observational checklists are much cheaper to print
options.D: Questionnaires cannot be used in a hospital setting

explanation: Direct observation captures real behavior, avoiding the bias or forgetfulness that comes with self-reporting. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is mainly responsible for making the detrusor muscle contract during urination?

options.A: Norepinephrine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key player here! It binds to receptors on the bladder wall to trigger that squeezing action. You're doing great.

question: Which health worker is primarily responsible for managing complex surgical deliveries in the team?

options.A: Obstetrician/Gynecologist
options.B: Pharmacy technician
options.C: Midwife
options.D: Community Health Extension Worker

explanation: An obstetrician is a physician specialist trained to handle complex surgical interventions like cesarean sections. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h3)

question: What kind of infections are treated using antibacterial drugs?

options.A: Bacterial infections
options.B: Parasitic infections
options.C: Fungal infections
options.D: Viral infections

explanation: Spot on! Antibacterials are designed specifically to target bacteria, while leaving viruses and fungi alone.

question: What is the main job of the rugae inside the vaginal canal?

options.A: To constantly secrete lubricating hormones
options.B: To let the vagina stretch wide during childbirth
options.C: To trap bacteria and stop infections
options.D: To produce the monthly period blood

explanation: Well done! Those little folds (rugae) act like an accordion, giving extra tissue so the vagina can safely stretch during delivery.

question: A patient receiving regular opioid doses is difficult to wake up and speaks in a sleepy whisper. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Increase the intravenous fluid rate to flush the drug out faster
options.B: Administer a full emergency dose of IV naloxone immediately
options.C: Document that the patient is sleeping peacefully and leave them alone
options.D: Withhold the next scheduled dose and assess breathing depth

explanation: Excessive sedation precedes respiratory depression; holding the medication and checking breathing protects the patient from dangerous overdose. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h7)

question: Why are tiny finger-like projections called chorionic villi so important for a developing baby?

options.A: They prevent the mother's immune system from rejecting the fetus.
options.B: They greatly increase surface area for nutrient and gas exchange.
options.C: They produce all the amniotic fluid found in the amniotic sac.
options.D: They form the muscular walls of the uterus to prepare for labor.

explanation: Think of chorionic villi like the branching roots of a tree; their massive surface area makes it easy for the baby to absorb oxygen and food from the mother.

question: A patient scheduled for a thoracocentesis looks anxious and asks if they can talk or move around. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Advise the patient to lie completely flat on their back to relax
options.B: Tell the patient they can move freely as long as the doctor is wearing gloves
options.C: Explain that staying still and avoiding talking or coughing is important to protect the lung
options.D: Reassure them that moving around helps the fluid drain much faster

explanation: Clear instructions help the patient understand that movement increases the risk of accidental lung injury. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h4)

question: How does a relaxed, sagging abdominal wall (pendulous abdomen) commonly affect the baby's position late in pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the baby's head from fitting properly into the pelvis.
options.B: It forces the baby into a permanent footling breech position.
options.C: It speeds up the opening of the cervix weeks before labor begins.
options.D: It causes the placenta to detach prematurely from the uterine wall.

explanation: When weak tummy muscles let the uterus lean too far forward, the baby's head doesn't line up right with the pelvic opening, making it harder for the head to engage naturally.

question: What makes hepatorenal syndrome different from regular kidney failure?

options.A: Kidneys stop working because of high blood sugar
options.B: It only happens to people with healthy livers
options.C: It causes permanent physical damage to kidney tissue
options.D: The kidneys fail due to altered blood flow, not physical injury

explanation: Spot on! Hepatorenal syndrome happens because of severe blood circulation changes caused by liver issues—the kidney tissue itself isn't physically damaged at first. Excellent clinical insight!

question: Which action is strictly forbidden when handling used injection needles to prevent injuries?

options.A: Recapping needles by hand
options.B: Placing needles in a puncture-resistant bin
options.C: Reporting a sharps stick immediately
options.D: Carrying a tray with a used syringe

explanation: Correct! Never recap needles by hand—it's a leading cause of accidental needlestick injuries in the clinic.

question: How does severe dehydration usually trick the numbers on a patient's blood lab results?

options.A: It artificially raises the values.
options.B: It destroys all proteins instantly.
options.C: It artificially lowers the values.
options.D: It has no effect on lab values.

explanation: Less fluid in the blood vessels means the remaining substances are more concentrated, making lab counts look higher than they actually are!

question: When should you ideally start planning for a neurological client's discharge?

options.A: Only after all therapy sessions are finished
options.B: The evening before the client goes home
options.C: When the doctor finally writes the discharge order
options.D: On the day of hospital admission

explanation: It sounds early, but starting day one gives you enough breathing room to sort out equipment, teach family members, and prep the home before discharge day sneaks up!

question: Your patient's GCS score keeps dropping over the last two hours. What should this trend tell you immediately?

options.A: Normal tiredness at the end of the day
options.B: A minor hearing loss developing in the patient
options.C: Worsening neurological status and potential brain swelling
options.D: A temporary reaction to hospital food

explanation: A falling GCS score is a serious warning sign. It means brain function is declining and you must act fast!

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard health interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on emotional support and coping
options.B: Counselling relies exclusively on closed-ended questions
options.C: Counselling replaces all physical health assessments
options.D: Counselling is only performed by hospital chaplains

explanation: Great thinking! While an interview gathers facts, counselling helps patients process feelings and handle health challenges.

question: Why should a nurse manager look for the root cause before penalizing an error?

options.A: Many errors are caused by broken workflows rather than careless staff
options.B: Punishing staff members is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Hospital labor unions forbid managers from talking to individual nurses
options.D: Root cause analysis is only required for surgical complications

explanation: If a faulty system or bad equipment caused the mistake, punishing the nurse won't stop it from happening again to someone else.

question: How does cerebrospinal fluid protect the brain from injury?

options.A: By providing buoyancy that reduces the net weight of the brain
options.B: By locking the brain rigidly in place to prevent all movement
options.C: By generating electrical currents that power nerve conduction
options.D: By inflating the skull bones to create a larger cranial vault

explanation: You got it! Floating in this fluid makes the heavy brain feel much lighter, keeping delicate tissue safe from being crushed by its own weight against the skull.

question: Which mechanism allows one drug to help another enter cells more easily?

options.A: Destroying all circulating white blood cells
options.B: Altering cell membrane permeability
options.C: Increasing the patient's daily fluid intake
options.D: Speeding up normal kidney filtration rates

explanation: By changing how easy it is to pass through the cell membrane, one drug acts like an opening wedge, helping its partner medication get inside.

question: A nurse is preparing to start a blood transfusion for an adult patient. Which intravenous solution should be used to prime the Y-tubing?

options.A: 5% dextrose in water
options.B: 0.45% sodium chloride
options.C: 0.9% sodium chloride
options.D: Lactated Ringer's solution

explanation: Normal saline (0.9% sodium chloride) is isotonic and compatible with red blood cells, preventing hemolysis that other solutions might cause. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h6)

question: You find a weeping trader sitting alone after a market fire. What is your best first move using PFA?

options.A: Insist that the trader explain the exact sequence of how the fire started
options.B: Approach calmly, offer a safe space, and listen to immediate practical concerns
options.C: Refer the trader directly to a psychiatric hospital for formal psychotherapy
options.D: Administer a strong oral sedative to prevent immediate panic attacks

explanation: Great nurse instinct! PFA isn't about interrogation or rushing to drugs. It's about a calm, safe presence and listening to what they need right now.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended preventive action for nurses?

options.A: Identifying children at high risk during routine health visits
options.B: Performing minor cuts in the clinic to prevent severe home procedures
options.C: Collaborating with community leaders to protect young girls
options.D: Counseling families about the legal and health dangers of FGM

explanation: Nurses must never perform FGM under any circumstances, as medicalisation is unethical and illegal. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which lab tests are most important to monitor regularly for patients taking long-term multi-drug therapy?

options.A: Liver enzymes and kidney function tests
options.B: Stool culture and electrolyte balance
options.C: Thyroid hormones and iron levels
options.D: Complete blood count and blood type

explanation: Spot on! Since the liver and kidneys do the heavy lifting of processing and clearing drugs, keeping an eye on their lab values is our best way to catch early signs of strain or toxicity.

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed blood-borne viruses
options.B: Patients admitted to the surgical ward only
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.D: Individuals showing visible signs of a fever

explanation: Standard precautions assume any patient fluid could carry pathogens, protecting nurses and patients alike during every encounter. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle common myths and rumors about modern birth control?

options.A: Telling clients to rely solely on traditional calendar methods
options.B: Agreeing that contraceptives cause permanent internal damage
options.C: Providing accurate, evidence-based education tailored to the client
options.D: Withholding information about long-acting reversible methods

explanation: Great nursing insight! Patient education clears up fear and empowers clients to make healthy choices.

question: What is selective reporting in research?

options.A: Using pseudonyms to protect the identity of study participants
options.B: Aligning numbers by their decimal points in a table
options.C: Highlighting only supportive data while hiding contradictory results
options.D: Choosing between a bar chart and a statistical table

explanation: Selective reporting is an unethical practice where researchers suppress unfavorable findings to present a biased picture. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main physical effect of a CNS depressant drug?

options.A: Enhancing skeletal muscle contraction strength
options.B: Slowing down brain activity and neural signaling
options.C: Increasing heart rate and blood pressure rapidly
options.D: Stimulating excess production of red blood cells

explanation: CNS depressants calm the central nervous system down by slowing down brain and spinal cord activity, which helps with sleep or anxiety.

question: A community health nurse in a Nigerian riverine village wants to run a program against paragonimiasis. What should be the top priority?

options.A: Screening pregnant mothers for gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Holding health talks on safe food preparation by local rivers
options.C: Distributing mosquito nets to all households in the community
options.D: Administering routine oral polio vaccines to infants

explanation: Brilliant choice! Focusing on local dietary habits and safe cooking directly targets how the infection is actually spread in that community.

question: What should the nurse do first before starting a physical examination?

options.A: Ask the family members to leave the hospital room
options.B: Prepare the environment and gather needed equipment
options.C: Perform a deep tissue palpation of the abdomen
options.D: Administer prescribed pain medications immediately

explanation: Organizing your tools and space beforehand prevents interruptions and keeps the patient calm and comfortable. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is it dangerous to pour household cleaning chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: Bottled drinks cannot hold the weight of heavy industrial-strength soap
options.B: It causes the chemical solution to evaporate and lose its cleaning power completely
options.C: The plastic material used in beverage bottles reacts poorly with standard water
options.D: It increases the risk of accidental ingestion by mistaking the chemical for a drink

explanation: That's right! Putting chemicals in drink bottles is a major cause of accidental poisoning because someone might easily mistake it for a refreshing drink.

question: Why did older medical books divide these drugs into major and minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Depending on whether the patient is male or female
options.B: Based on how strong the drug is and how serious the condition is
options.C: According to the physical weight of the drug tablet
options.D: To separate drugs made from plants from lab-made ones

explanation: Think of major tranquilizers as handling severe mental disturbances, while minor ones manage milder anxiety. Simple and clear!

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to advocate for food policy changes?

options.A: They are primarily responsible for writing national agricultural laws
options.B: They witness the direct health impacts of poor nutrition in clinical practice
options.C: They control the financial budgets of international food agencies
options.D: They manage the commercial distribution of imported grain

explanation: Nurses see malnutrition and diet-related disease daily, giving them firsthand evidence of policy needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: A patient with PCOS and insulin resistance is given metformin. What is the main goal of this drug for her?

options.A: O dissolve large fibroids in just a few days
options.B: To force early surgical menopause
options.C: To improve metabolism and lower high male hormone levels
options.D: To stop pelvic organs from dropping

explanation: Spot on! Metformin helps the body handle insulin better, which lowers insulin levels and stops the ovaries from making too many androgens.

question: When is it okay to leave a smart bed's wheel brakes unlocked?

options.A: When the patient is sleeping soundly through the night
options.B: Whenever the bed exit alarm system is fully armed
options.C: Only when the bed is actively being transported
options.D: During routine morning bed baths and linen changes

explanation: Always keep brakes locked! The only exception is when you are actively wheeling the bed down the hallway to a new room.

question: Why are pregnant women told to avoid unpasteurized dairy and deli meats?

options.A: These foods always cause immediate skin rashes
options.B: They are at high risk for dangerous Listeria infections
options.C: These items contain artificial food colors
options.D: Pregnant women cannot digest animal protein

explanation: You got it! Listeria is sneaky and can cross the placenta, causing serious harm to a pregnancy. That's why we always educate expectant mothers to steer clear!

question: Why is involving family members in dietary education so important for these patients?

options.A: Family members usually buy and prepare the food eaten at home
options.B: The family is legally responsible if the patient breaks the diet
options.C: Relatives must also follow a strict low protein diet together
options.D: It prevents the patient from cooking hot meals on the stove

explanation: Because household food preparation is often a shared or family duty, involving relatives ensures the prescribed diet is actually followed at home. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a neonatal bag-valve-mask (BVM) in your kit?

options.A: To give artificial breaths to a newborn who isn't breathing on their own
options.B: To clear meconium out of the baby's tummy during a checkup
options.C: To weigh the baby accurately in kilograms
options.D: To wrap the baby securely against cold drafts

explanation: The BVM lets you gently give lifesaving breaths to a struggling newborn until they start breathing all by themselves.

question: Why is protecting health information harder in a home setting than in a hospital?

options.A: Patients demand that their records be posted on the front door
options.B: Family members, visitors, and housemates are frequently present in the care area
options.C: Home health nurses are not bound by legal privacy rules
options.D: Hospitals do not have strict privacy laws

explanation: Spot on! Homes are busy places with people walking in and out, making it easy for others to accidentally overhear health matters or see your notes.

question: A patient on trial leave stops taking their medication and acts aggressively at home. What is the main advantage of trial leave status?

options.A: The hospital automatically discharges the patient to a prison facility
options.B: The team must wait until the next court date
options.C: The family is fined for failing to supervise
options.D: The patient can be readmitted quickly without a complex new admission process

explanation: Because the patient is still officially connected to the hospital during trial leave, bringing them back safely and quickly is much easier if symptoms flare up.

question: A nurse wants to test if a new handwashing technique actually lowers ward infection rates. What study design fits best?

options.A: Historical biography
options.B: Qualitative phenomenology
options.C: Philosophical essay
options.D: Quantitative experimental

explanation: Because you are tracking numbers (infection rates) and testing an intervention, you need a quantitative experimental approach!

question: Which chart is best for showing how patient vital signs change over time?

options.A: Frequency table
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Bar chart
options.D: Line graph

explanation: You got it! Whenever you want to track changes over a timeline—like hourly blood pressure readings—a line graph is your best friend.

question: What is a very common emotional worry for patients facing a terminal diagnosis?

options.A: Excitement about trying new experimental diets
options.B: Fear of becoming a burden to loved ones
options.C: Desire to return to full-time strenuous employment
options.D: Indifference toward family relationships

explanation: Patients with serious illnesses often carry a heavy heart, worrying about the physical, emotional, and financial strain they might put on their family. Empathy is our greatest tool!

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fresh scarification cut that is red, swollen, and draining pus. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Normal healing of deep skin tissue
options.B: An allergic reaction to sunlight
options.C: A healthy immune response to the ink
options.D: Bacterial contamination from unhygienic practices

explanation: Spot on! Pus and swelling are classic signs that bacteria entered the wound due to unsterile tools or dirty substances applied to the cut.

question: What is the correct first step when inspecting a patient's scalp?

options.A: Comb the hair vigorously to remove loose strands
options.B: Apply a medicated shampoo to check for lather
options.C: Part the hair in multiple areas to view the skin
options.D: Shave a small patch to inspect the follicle roots

explanation: To properly check scalp health, gently part the hair in different spots so you can clearly see the skin underneath for any issues. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a hysterosalpingography test during an infertility workup?

options.A: To count the total number of immature eggs remaining in the ovaries
options.B: To check the thyroid gland for signs of overactivity
options.C: To visualize the uterine cavity and check if fallopian tubes are open
options.D: To measure the exact daily progesterone levels in the blood

explanation: Awesome job! During this test, dye is put through the cervix so x-rays can show if the fluid flows nicely through the tubes. You're building solid practical knowledge!

question: Which tool is commonly used by nurses to check a patient's risk of developing pressure sores upon admission?

options.A: Apgar Score
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Braden Scale
options.D: Pain Numeric Rating Scale

explanation: The Braden Scale is your go-to clinical tool! It checks things like moisture, mobility, and nutrition to give you a clear score of a patient's pressure sore risk. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for nurses?

options.A: To manufacture vaccines in community health clinics
options.B: To punish hospitals that fail to report patient admissions
options.C: To prescribe antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.D: To systematically collect and analyze health data for disease trends

explanation: Surveillance keeps a close eye on disease patterns so we can catch outbreaks early and track down where germs are hiding.

question: Why is a knitted structure preferred over a woven fabric for a stockinette?

options.A: It completely stops all blood circulation
options.B: It sticks permanently to the patient's skin
options.C: It repels water completely like a raincoat
options.D: It stretches easily to fit body curves smoothly

explanation: The knit stitch allows the fabric to expand and conform tightly to irregular body shapes without forming wrinkles. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which physical sign tells you right away that a patient is getting dehydrated?

options.A: Flushed and warm skin
options.B: Moist, pink mucous membranes
options.C: Dry, cracked mucous membranes
options.D: Bounding peripheral pulses

explanation: Dry mouth and lips are classic, quick red flags that the body is low on water. Always check the mucous membranes during your assessments!

question: What is the main goal of a summative evaluation at the end of an IEC campaign?

options.A: To measure the final impact and changes in community health behavior
options.B: To replace traditional rulers with modern local government staff
options.C: To check if the printing budget was spent on the exact correct date
options.D: To decide which nurse should be transferred to another clinic

explanation: Summative evaluation happens at the 'summary' or end of the project to check: did our campaign actually work? Did health habits improve? [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: Which imaging scan is commonly used to stage lymphomas by checking for swollen lymph nodes?

options.A: Pulmonary function test
options.B: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.C: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
options.D: Electrocardiogram (ECG)

explanation: A CT scan gives clear, slice-by-slice pictures that show the size and location of lymph nodes and organs inside the body.

question: What does the abbreviation HAI stand for in nursing practice?

options.A: High acuity illness
options.B: Hygiene assessment indicator
options.C: Healthcare-associated infection
options.D: Hospital antiseptic index

explanation: HAIs are infections patients acquire while receiving medical treatment in a hospital or clinic facility. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)

question: A client with a new physical disability refuses their medications and seems very hopeless. What does this most likely point to?

options.A: Unaddressed emotional distress impacting their treatment plan
options.B: A simple misunderstanding of the medication dosage schedule
options.C: An allergic reaction to the newly prescribed drugs
options.D: Normal adjustment that requires no nursing intervention

explanation: When clients give up or refuse care, it's often a cry for help. Deep emotional pain can get right in the way of managing physical health.

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands use ducts to transport fluids to body surfaces.
options.B: Endocrine glands produce enzymes instead of chemical messengers.
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.
options.D: Endocrine glands only function during physical stress.

explanation: Remember: Endocrine means 'ductless'—they release their hormones straight into nearby blood vessels. Exocrine glands (like sweat or salivary glands) use ducts to send their products to a surface.

question: Which detail is most important for a home nurse to record during feeding visits?

options.A: Estimated percentage of meals eaten and weight trends
options.B: The exact brand of dishes used in the household
options.C: The grocery store prices of all purchased food
options.D: The names of visiting neighbors and friends

explanation: You got it! Tracking intake percentages and weight changes tells you clearly if the nutrition plan is working.

question: Why does the anaesthetist stay close to the patient's head during surgery?

options.A: To assist the surgeon with knot-tying and tissue retraction
options.B: To manage the airway and monitor breathing continuously
options.C: To clean blood off the surgical instruments during the operation
options.D: To count surgical instruments before the wound is closed

explanation: By staying right by the head, the anaesthetist can easily keep the airway open, give oxygen, and watch vital signs every second.

question: What does the 'Great Man' theory say about leadership?

options.A: Leadership qualities are inherited at birth
options.B: Anyone can learn to lead through weekend workshops
options.C: Only senior physicians are capable of guiding ward staff
options.D: Leadership depends entirely on the surrounding environment

explanation: The Great Man theory suggests that great leaders are born with natural talents, rather than trained. A bit old-school, but an important concept to know!

question: When is the best time for a patient to give a sputum sample?

options.A: At any random time during the afternoon shift
options.B: Early in the morning right after waking up
options.C: Immediately after eating a heavy midday meal
options.D: Right before going to sleep at night

explanation: First thing in the morning is golden! Mucus collects in the airways overnight, giving you a rich, concentrated sample from deep in the chest.

question: When reading a measuring tape, why is it important to look straight across at eye level instead of viewing it from an angle?

options.A: To avoid calibration error
options.B: To prevent longitudinal stretch error
options.C: To prevent parallax error
options.D: To avoid compression error

explanation: Looking at a scale from the side makes numbers look skewed. Reading straight across at eye level ensures your measurement is spot on!

question: Which of these actions goes AGAINST a nurse's ethical duties?

options.A: Sharing patient medical details on social media
options.B: Advocating for the best interests of the sick person
options.C: Protecting patient privacy and medical confidentiality
options.D: Respecting the cultural beliefs of every patient

explanation: Correct! Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing patient details online is a serious breach of ethics and professional trust.

question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.A: To prove a direct cause-and-effect relationship between two treatments
options.B: To accurately describe a situation or population without changing variables
options.C: To test a new medical drug against a standard placebo
options.D: To manipulate patient routines and measure the physical outcome

explanation: Think of descriptive research like taking a clear photograph: you are just capturing things exactly as they are in real life without meddling or changing anything. Great job! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is a major perk of getting your vitamins from real food instead of pills?

options.A: Pills are always completely fake and contain no actual vitamins
options.B: Whole foods provide fiber and a complex nutritional matrix
options.C: Whole foods cost nothing at all to produce or purchase
options.D: Pills take up to a week to dissolve in the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! Whole foods come with extra bonuses like fiber and natural plant compounds that supplements just can't copy.
